For example, open a pull request from your feature branch into `main` and merge it. Lovable then picks up those commits.\nL625:   * Switch the synced branch in Lovable. In your project’s GitHub settings, select the branch where your commits live. Lovable starts editing and syncing that branch instead, and your commits will appear.\nL626: \nL627: I pushed to the synced branch, but the commits don\'t appear in Lovable and the sync status says GitHub is ahead.\nL628: Lovable pulls your changes when GitHub notifies it about a push to the synced branch. If that notification never arrives, the commits from that push don’t appear in Lovable, and Lovable doesn’t pull them later without a new notification. The \ue200cite\ue20261†sync status\ue201 card in the project’s GitHub settings shows GitHub is N commits ahead of Lovable until the next sync.Reconnect doesn’t fix this. It appears only when the connection itself has a problem, and it restores access to the repository without pulling commits.\nL629: Re-check on the sync status card compares the branches again and doesn’t sync anything either.To make Lovable pull the missing commits, push a new commit to the synced branch. Any push works, including an empty commit:\nL630: \nL631:     `git commit --allow-empty -m "Trigger Lovable sync"\nL632:     git push\nL633:     `\nL634: Lovable then syncs the branch to its current state on GitHub, which includes the earlier commits.Before you push, confirm the branch and the state of your Lovable edits:\nL635:   * You’re pushing to the repository and branch shown in \ue200cite\ue20255†Project settings → Git\ue201 → GitHub. Commits on other branches don’t sync.\nL636:   * Your latest Lovable edits are already in the repository on GitHub. If the sync status says Lovable and GitHub have diverged, the push replaces Lovable’s version of the branch with the GitHub version, and the project no longer contains edits made only in Lovable. Lovable saves a backup first, and the project owner can \ue200cite\ue20276†restore it\ue201 from the notice in the editor or in Project settings → Git.\nL637: If the commits still don’t appear after a new push, contact \ue200cite\ue20277†Lovable Support†lovable.dev\ue201 .\nL638: I see a "lovable-fallback" branch in the branch picker.\nL639: \nL640: Someone deleted the synced branch on GitHub. Lovable automatically switched the project to a new branch called `lovable-fallback` so that you can continue editing. Your repository is otherwise unchanged.Pick another branch or recreate the original branch. After you switch away, you can leave or delete `lovable-fallback` in GitHub.\nL641: \nL642: Sync stopped working after I added a large file.\nL643: GitHub rejects pushes that contain files larger than 100 MB. When this happens, your project’s GitHub settings show the error “Your project contains files that exceed the maximum file size limit (100 MB)” together with a list of the affected files, after a few failed sync attempts.To fix it, delete the listed files from your project (or ask Lovable to remove them) and let the sync retry.\nL644: If the push keeps failing after the files are gone, an oversized file is stuck in the repository’s history, and history cleanup requires help from \ue200cite\ue20277†Lovable Support†lovable.dev\ue201 .Separately, Lovable itself cannot save files larger than 10 MB into your project. Files you push from your own computer can be larger (up to GitHub’s limits) and sync into Lovable, but Lovable cannot edit those files afterwards: any Lovable change that touches a file over 10 MB fails.\nL645: For large media, ask Lovable to “Migrate large files to CDN assets”. See the \ue200cite\ue20278†chat page FAQ\ue201 for details.\nL646: My push from Lovable ended up on a "lovable-sync" branch instead of the synced branch.\nL647: GitHub rejected the push to your synced branch, most often because of branch protection rules or because someone pushed a conflicting change that Lovable could not apply your work on top of. To avoid losing your work, Lovable pushed it to a branch named `lovable-sync` instead, and your project’s GitHub settings show “Your changes conflict with commits on `<your branch>` and could not be merged automatically. They were pushed to the branch `lovable-sync` instead.\nL648: Merge that branch into `<your branch>` to apply them.”Open that branch on GitHub, review the changes, and merge them into your protected branch through your usual review process.When a later push is rejected too, Lovable adds those changes to the same `lovable-sync` branch. If you’ve added your own commits to `lovable-sync`, Lovable leaves them untouched and pushes to a new branch named `lovable-sync-<timestamp>` instead. Review and merge that branch the same way.\nL649: ##\nL650: \nL651: \ue200cite\ue20259†\u200b\ue201 L652: \nL653: FAQ\nL654: \nL655: Do I need to know GitHub to use Git sync?\nL656: \nL657: No. Set up Git sync once, and GitHub safely stores your code.You only need to learn GitHub’s features if you want to do more advanced things such as branching, pull requests, or CI/CD.\nL658: \nL659: Is the repository Lovable creates public or private?\nL660: \nL661: Repositories created by Lovable are private by default, on every plan. Nobody can see your code on GitHub unless you change the repository’s visibility yourself in GitHub’s settings.\nL662: Do I need GitHub just to download my code?\nL663: \nL664: No. On paid plans you can download your code directly from Lovable: use the Download codebase section in Project settings → Git, or click Download codebase at the bottom of the \ue200cite\ue20248†Code editor\ue201 file tree sidebar.GitHub is for ongoing two-way sync and collaboration, not just for getting a copy of your code.\nL665: \nL666: What\'s the difference between github.com, GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and GitHub Enterprise Server?\nL667:   * github.com is the standard hosted GitHub service and is available on all plans.\nL668:   * GitHub Enterprise Cloud (data residency) uses a `*.ghe.com` hostname so your data stays in a specific region. It uses the Lovable-managed GitHub app. Available on the Enterprise plan.\nL669:   * GitHub Enterprise Server is GitHub running on your own infrastructure. You register your own copy of the Lovable GitHub app inside your organization. Available on the Enterprise plan.\nL670: What permissions does the Lovable GitHub app request?\nL671: \nL672: The Lovable GitHub app requests:\nL673:   * Contents (write): Read and write code in your repositories.\nL674:   * Metadata (read): Basic repository information.\nL675:   * Pull requests (write): Open and update pull requests.\nL676:   * Workflows (write): Manage GitHub Actions workflow files.\nL677:   * Administration (write): Create new repositories under your account or organization.\nL678: The app subscribes to push, pull_request, repository, and delete events to keep Lovable in sync with GitHub.\nL679: \nL680: What happens if I rename, move, or delete my GitHub repository?\nL681: It depends on the change:\nL682:   * Rename the repository: Sync continues. Lovable detects the rename and updates the connection automatically.\nL683:   * Transfer the repository to another account or organization: Sync continues when your Lovable workspace also has a GitHub connection for the new owner. Lovable moves the project to that connection and updates the repository link. Without such a connection, Lovable disconnects the project. To resume syncing, add a connection for the new owner and connect the project again, which creates a new repository, or transfer the repository back to its original owner.\nL684:   * Delete the repository: The connection breaks and the project stops syncing. You can \ue200cite\ue20275†restore the deleted repository on GitHub†docs.github.com\ue201 to resume syncing, or disconnect and reconnect the project to create a new repository.\nL685: What happens if I rename my GitHub username or organization?\nL686: \nL687: Sync continues. GitHub notifies Lovable of the rename, and Lovable updates the connection to the new name. The connection in Workspace settings → Git shows the new name.\nL688: \nL689: What happens if I transfer my project to another workspace?\nL690: The GitHub connection breaks during the transfer. Lovable shows a warning before you confirm. After the transfer, your repository stays on GitHub but is no longer linked to Lovable.To resume syncing, set up a GitHub connection in the destination workspace and reconnect the project. Lovable creates a new repository on reconnect.\nL691: \nL692: How can I switch to a different GitHub account or organization?\nL693: \nL694: You can’t change the linked GitHub account on an existing project.As a workaround:\nL695:   1. Disconnect the project from GitHub in the project’s GitHub settings.\nL696:   2. Reconnect the project and choose a different installation during setup.\nL697: Lovable creates a new repository. The original repository stays on GitHub but is no longer linked to Lovable.\nL698: \nL699: Can I use multiple GitHub accounts or organizations?\nL700: Yes. A workspace can have multiple GitHub connections, each pointing to a different personal account or organization, and these can be on github.com, your data residency instance, or your GitHub Enterprise Server. Each Lovable project is then linked to one repository within one of those installations.\nL701: \nL702: Can I disconnect from GitHub?\nL703: Yes. Workspace or project admins and owners can \ue200cite\ue20270†disconnect a project from a GitHub repository\ue201 at any time in the project’s GitHub settings.Your repository stays on GitHub, but syncing stops. If you reconnect later, a new repository is created.\nL704: \nL705: Can I import an existing GitHub repo into Lovable?\nL706: \nL707: No. You can only export from Lovable to GitHub, not the other way around.\nL708: \nL709: Can I edit a non-default branch from inside Lovable?\nL710: Yes. The branch picker in your project’s GitHub repository connection lets you \ue200cite\ue20263†switch to any branch\ue201 in your repository. You can also \ue200cite\ue20264†create a new branch\ue201 directly from the picker. Lovable forks from the branch you’re currently editing, so switch to your intended starting point (usually `main`) first.\nL711: \nL712: Are commits made by Lovable attributed to me?\nL713: \nL714: Commits made by Lovable are authored by the Lovable GitHub app identity:\nL715:   * `lovable-dev[bot]` for github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud\nL716:   * `<your-app-name>[bot]` for GitHub Enterprise Server\nL717: Commits are also co-attributed to the workspace member who triggered them, using the email address on their connected GitHub account, or GitHub’s `noreply` format when that address is not available. That line is absent for members who have not connected a GitHub account. To record who triggered each commit regardless, see \ue200cite\ue20269†Commit attribution\ue201 .\nL718: My GitHub Enterprise Server is behind a VPN or firewall. Will it work?\nL719: \nL720: Only if Lovable’s public IP ranges can reach your instance. Lovable needs network access to your GitHub Enterprise Server to push code and receive webhook events.\nL721: \nL722: Where is my data stored for GitHub Enterprise Cloud (data residency)?\nL723: With data residency, repository data and webhook traffic stay within the GitHub region tied to your `*.ghe.com` hostname. Lovable’s backend connects to that hostname from the IP ranges shown in the setup wizard. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Wall time: 0.0979 seconds\nOutput:'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '# Tab Capability: cdp\nRaw Chrome DevTools Protocol access in browser for development use. Prefer higher-level Browser Use APIs. Navigate a fresh tab to its intended HTTP or HTTPS page before the first CDP command. Raw CDP access is scoped to the tab\'s current web origin. To observe an action, call `readEvents()` to capture `cursor`, perform the action, then read from that cursor with `afterSequence`. Continue from each returned cursor while `hasMore` is true; `truncated` means older events were evicted. Reuse the same filters while paging. Discover child target selectors from `Target.attachedToTarget` events. If you directly modify page content or browser state through CDP, outside ordinary navigation or UI interaction, and leave that change in place, tell the user what changed in the final response.\n\n```ts\nconst capability = await tab.capabilities.get("cdp");\n\ntype CdpEventsOptions = {\n  afterSequence?: number; // Return events after this cursor; omit to start at the current position.\n  limit?: number; // Maximum number of events to return, from 1 to 1000.\n  methods?: Array<string>; // Return only these CDP event methods; must not be empty.\n  target?: CdpTarget; // Filter by child target, including buffered events after it detaches.\n  timeoutMs?: number; // Wait up to this many milliseconds for the first match.\n};\n\ntype CdpCommandParams = Record<string, unknown>;\n\ntype CdpSendOptions = {\n  target?: CdpTarget; // An attached child target; omit to send the command to the tab itself.\n  timeoutMs?: number; // Maximum command wait in milliseconds.\n};\n\ntype CdpTarget = { sessionId: string; targetId?: never } | { sessionId?: never; targetId: string };\n\ninterface CdpTabCapability {\n  readEvents(options?: CdpEventsOptions): Promise<{ cursor: number; events: Array<{ method: string; params?: Record<string, unknown>; sequence: number; source: { extensionId?: string; sessionId?: string; tabId?: number; targetId?: string } }>; hasMore: boolean; truncated: boolean }>; // Read buffered CDP events, optionally waiting for the first match.\n  send(method: string, params?: CdpCommandParams, options?: CdpSendOptions): Promise<unknown>; // Send a permitted CDP command to this tab or an attached child target.\n}\n```\n'}]

Other triggers enforce\\r\\n    -- the allowed statuses; this exception never creates or rebinds access.\\r\\n    if TG_OP=\'UPDATE\' and OLD.type=\'activity\' and OLD.source_table=\'reading_center\' and OLD.source_id=\'library\'\\r\\n      and NEW.student_id is not distinct from OLD.student_id\\r\\n      and NEW.created_by is not distinct from OLD.created_by\\r\\n      and NEW.visible_to_student is not distinct from OLD.visible_to_student\\r\\n      and NEW.unlock_at is not distinct from OLD.unlock_at then\\r\\n      return NEW;\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n  end if;\\r\\n  v_activity := NEW.source_table = \'activity_assignments\' or NEW.type = \'activity\';\\r\\n  -- Existing orphan mirrors are historical data. Unrelated edits do not grant\\r\\n  -- access; newly visible or rebound mirrors must satisfy the source gate.\\r\\n  if TG_OP = \'UPDATE\' then\\r\\n    v_activity := coalesce(v_activity,false) or OLD.source_table = \'activity_assignments\' or OLD.type = \'activity\';\\r\\n    if NEW.visible_to_student is not distinct from OLD.visible_to_student\\r\\n       and NEW.source_table is not distinct from OLD.source_table\\r\\n       and NEW.source_id is not distinct from OLD.source_id\\r\\n       and NEW.type is not distinct from OLD.type\\r\\n       and NEW.student_id is not distinct from OLD.student_id then\\r\\n      return NEW;\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n  end if;\\r\\n  if NEW.visible_to_student and v_activity then\\r\\n    if NEW.source_id is null or\\r\\n       (NEW.source_table is distinct from \'activity_assignments\' and NEW.type is distinct from \'activity\') then\\r\\n      raise exception \'Visible Activity mirror source cannot be cleared\' using errcode = \'42501\';\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n    select revoked_at, student_id into v_revoked, v_student\\r\\n      from public.activity_assignments where id::text = NEW.source_id for share;\\r\\n    if not found or v_revoked is not null or v_student is distinct from NEW.student_id then\\r\\n      raise exception \'Activity mirror must name an available source for this student\' using errcode = \'42501\';\\r\\n    end if;\\r\\n  end if;\\r\\n  return NEW;\\r\\nend;\\r\\n$function$;\\r\\ncommit;\\r\\n"}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"rows":[{"id":"689b3dfb-e18b-43fe-9b28-b2f42c10f541","status":"in_progress","updated_at":"2026-10-14 02:05:32.833396+00","visible_to_student":false}]}'}]
